sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Jane Austen** (1775–1817), celebrated English novelist known for domestic realism and social satire.
**Pride and Prejudice** (Originally written as **First Impressions** in 1797; published anonymously in **1813**).
**Elizabeth Bennet** (second eldest daughter, witty and intelligent) and **Fitzwilliam Darcy** (wealthy, proud landowner).
The overcoming of initial misjudgments (**pride** on Darcy's part, **prejudice** on Elizabeth's part) leading to mutual love and marriage.
**Class and Social Status**, **Reputation and Honor**, **Marriage and Economics**, **Gender Roles**.
High-frequency topic in **UP Assistant Teacher (English)** exams regarding characters, publication years, quotes, and Austen's style.

items.title: 1. Biographical Context of **Jane Austen**
items.content:
• Born in **Steventon, Hampshire**, on **December 16, 1775** to rector **George Austen** and Cassandra Austen.
• Lived a quiet domestic life, observing the nuances of the British landed gentry and clergy.
• Never married, relying heavily on family support for her writing career.
• Published all her major novels **anonymously** during her lifetime (attributed as 'By a Lady').
• Died on **July 18, 1817** in **Winchester** at the age of 41.
• **Mnemonic for Key Novels:** **A**ll **E**nglish **M**en **P**refer **N**ice **S**isters (**A**bbey [Northanger], **E**mma, **M**ansfield Park, **P**ride and Prejudice, **N**orthanger [Persuasion note: use P for Persuasion], **S**ense and Sensibility).

items.title: 2. The Novel of Manners & **Social Satire**
items.content:
• **Novel of Manners:** Focuses on the customs, behaviors, habits, and social codes of a specific social class (**English landed gentry**).
• **Social Satire:** Austen mocks the obsession with wealth, aristocratic birth, entailment laws, and marriage markets.
• Use of **Free Indirect Discourse**: Blends third-person narration with the inner thoughts and voice of characters (especially Elizabeth Bennet).
• Irony and Wit: Opens with one of the most famous satirical lines in English literature regarding wealthy bachelors and wives.
• Focus on domestic spheres rather than grand historical or political events.

items.title: 3. Major Themes: **Pride**, **Prejudice**, and **Class**
items.content:
• **Pride:** Represented primarily by **Darcy** (pride of birth, wealth, and social superiority) and secondarily by Elizabeth (intellectual pride).
• **Prejudice:** Represented by **Elizabeth** (hasty judgments based on first impressions and gossip from Wickham) and Darcy's snobbery.
• **Social Class & Entailment:** Explores the vulnerability of women under strict **primogeniture** laws (Longbourn estate entailed to **Mr. Collins**).
• **Marriage:** Examines marriages of convenience (**Charlotte Lucas** and **Mr. Collins**), mercenary marriages (**Lydia** and **Wickham**), and marriages of true affection (**Elizabeth** and **Darcy**).

items.title: 4. Character Dynamics and Foil Techniques
items.content:
• **Elizabeth Bennet** acts as a foil to her sister **Jane Bennet** (Elizabeth is sharp and skeptical; Jane is universally charitable and optimistic).
• **Mr. Darcy** acts as a foil to **George Wickham** (Darcy is honorable and principled beneath coldness; Wickham is charming and deceptive beneath superficial grace).
• **Mrs. Bennet** highlights the frantic desperation of mothers with unmarried daughters in a society dependent on male inheritance.
• **Mr. Collins** satirizes sycophancy, religious hypocrisy, and blind obedience to aristocratic patronage (**Lady Catherine de Bourgh**).

items.title: 5. Literary Style, Tone, and Irony
items.content:
• Mastery of **verbal irony**, situational irony, and dramatic irony.
• Epistolary elements embedded within the narrative (crucial letters from **Darcy** to Elizabeth, and **Mr. Collins** to the Bennets).
• Compact scope: Austen famously described her work as a 'little bit (two inches wide) of ivory on which I work with so fine a brush.'
• Focus on moral growth, self-awareness, and emotional maturity (**bildungsroman** elements for both Elizabeth and Darcy).

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: First published novel; contrasts emotional excess with practical prudence.
Masterpiece of social comedy; originally titled 'First Impressions' (1797).
Explores morality, theatricals, and quiet endurance through Fanny Price.
Comedy of misplaced matchmaking and self-deception.
Satire on Gothic romance novels; written around 1798-1799.
Austen's most mature and melancholic novel about second chances in love.
Epistolary novella featuring a manipulative, cunning female protagonist.

sections.title: Major Characters and Roles
rows: Witty, independent, quick-witted; overcomes prejudice against Darcy.
Wealthy owner of Pemberley; initially proud, later humble and generous.
Deceitful, charming scoundrel; elopes with **Lydia Bennet**.
Frivolous, reckless, flirtatious; marries Wickham hastily.
Arrogant, overbearing aristocrat; patroness of **Rosings Park**.
Mr. Bennet is cynical and detached; Mrs. Bennet is neurotic and match-making.

sections.title: Famous Quotes and Sources
rows: "It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife."

"Vanity is a very different thing from pride, though the words are often used synonymously. A person may be proud without being vain. Pride relates more to our opinion of ourselves, vanity to what we would have others think of us."
Explaining character psychology in **Pride and Prejudice**.
"I could easily forgive his pride, if he had not mortified mine."
Discussing Darcy's initial rejection at the Meryton ball.

Realization of his flaw after receiving Elizabeth's scathing letter.

Stating his rigid standards of judgment early in the novel.

items.term: Trick 1: The Bennet Sisters (Order from Eldest to Youngest)
items.definition: Use the mnemonic **JELK-L**: **J**ane, **E**lizabeth, **L**ydia, **K**atherine (Kitty), **L**ydia? Wait, use **JEL-KM**: **J**ane (Eldest), **E**lizabeth (Second), **L**ydia (Youngest - wait, Mary is 3rd!). Correct Order: **J**ane, **E**lizabeth, **M**ary, **K**atherine (Kitty), **L**ydia. Mnemonic: **J**ust **E**at **M**angoes **K**ept **L**ocal (**J**ane, **E**lizabeth, **M**ary, **K**atherine, **L**ydia).

items.term: Trick 2: Original Title of Pride and Prejudice
items.definition: Remember **F.P.** - **F**irst **P**rimary/Impressions became **P**ride and **P**rejudice.
Remember pairings with starting letters: **P**emberley = **P**hysical/Darcy (**P** & **D**); **N**etherfield = **N**ew/Bingley (**N** & **B**); **L**ongbourn = **L**ocal/Bennets (**L** & **B**).
Think of **1813** as **18** (age of majority) plus **13** (lucky/unlucky first impression).
Acronym **S-P-E-M-M-N**: **S**ense & Sensibility, **P**ride & Prejudice, **E**mma, **M**ansfield Park, **M**urray? No, **N**orthanger Abbey, **P**ersuasion. (S-P-E-M-N-P).
**W**ickham and **W**Lady Catherine = **W**rongdoers who create tension.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing First Impressions with Published Title
items.definition: Students often think 'First Impressions' was published. **Correction:** It was the original manuscript title rejected in 1797 and later heavily revised into **Pride and Prejudice** (1813).

items.term: Mistake 2: Assuming Elizabeth Bennet is the Eldest
items.definition: Elizabeth is the **second** eldest daughter. **Jane Bennet** is the eldest and most beautiful sister.
Mr. Collins's patroness is **Lady Catherine de Bourgh**, NOT Miss Bingley or Mrs. Hurst.

items.term: Mistake 4: Believing Darcy and Elizabeth Married First
items.definition: Jane and Bingley actually marry first in narrative timeline, followed by Elizabeth and Darcy, and finally Lydia and Wickham.
Jane Austen **never** published under her own name during her lifetime; her books were credited to 'A Lady' or 'By the Author of Sense and Sensibility'.
Wickham elopes with **Lydia Bennet**, NOT Georgiana Darcy (though he attempted to elope with Georgiana previously).
The novel opens with the famous satirical premise regarding wealthy bachelors and marriage.
Darcy snubs Elizabeth, wounding her pride and creating mutual prejudice.
Charles Bingley instantly falls for Jane Bennet, but his sisters and Darcy intervene to separate them.
Mr. Collins proposes to Elizabeth; when rejected, he immediately proposes to her friend **Charlotte Lucas**.
George Wickham lies to Elizabeth about Darcy cheating him out of his inheritance, fueling her hatred for Darcy.
Darcy proposes to Elizabeth while insulting her lower social connections; Elizabeth angrily rejects him.
Darcy gives Elizabeth a letter revealing Wickham's villainy and Lydia's narrow escape, shattering Elizabeth's prejudice.
Visiting Darcy's estate at **Pemberley**, Elizabeth sees proof of his true character and generosity.
Lydia elopes with Wickham, threatening the entire Bennet family with social ruin.
Darcy secretly tracks down Lydia and Wickham, pays off Wickham's debts, and forces them to marry, saving the Bennet family honor.
Lady Catherine confronts Elizabeth; Elizabeth stands her ground; Darcy realizes Elizabeth's feelings have changed.
The novel concludes with the marriages of **Jane and Bingley** and **Elizabeth and Darcy**.

upscNotes.content: For UP Assistant Teacher exams, memorize the exact publication years of all six major novels by Jane Austen, as chronological sorting questions are frequently asked.
Pay close attention to character relationships and estate names (Pemberley, Netherfield, Rosings, Longbourn) as matching-type questions are common.
Examiners often trap students by attributing Darcy's famous opening line or quotes to Elizabeth or the narrator. Always verify quote speakers.
Do not confuse the original manuscript title 'First Impressions' with 'Northanger Abbey' or 'Sense and Sensibility'.

keyTakeaways: Pride and Prejudice was published in **1813** after being originally titled **First Impressions** in 1797.
The novel is a quintessential **Novel of Manners** and **Social Satire** set in the **Regency Era**.
Central characters **Elizabeth Bennet** and **Fitzwilliam Darcy** overcome mutual pride and prejudice before uniting.
Jane Austen published all her works **anonymously** during her lifetime.
Key subplots include **Charlotte Lucas** marrying **Mr. Collins** for economic security and **Lydia's elopement** with **Wickham**.
Darcy's estate is **Pemberley**, Bingley's is **Netherfield Park**, and the Bennets live at **Longbourn**.
